summary: Updates RFC 4181, Guidelines for Authors and Reviewers of MIB Documents, to recognize the creation of the IETF Trust. It is a Best Current Practice.

plainLanguage.summary: This Best Current Practice changes the name in copyright notice templates in RFC 4181. The templates now say "The IETF Trust" where they previously said "The Internet Society".

questions: why did rfc 4181 need an update
subtitle: A focused update to RFC 4181's copyright notice templates for the IETF Trust.

tldr.problem: RFC 4181's copyright notice templates named the Internet Society after the IETF Trust had been created.
tldr.mechanism: The update replaces each occurrence of "The Internet Society" with "The IETF Trust" in Section 3.7's templates.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4181's templates align with the copyright notice changes recorded in RFC 4748. The RFC says the change has no impact on Internet security.

today: RFC 4841 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 4181. The unit metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes RFC 4841.

sections.title: Why RFC 4181 Needed an Update
sections.content: RFC 4841 updates RFC 4181, the guidelines for authors and reviewers of MIB documents. It brings those guidelines into line with copyright notice changes published in RFC 4748 to recognize the creation of the IETF Trust.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 4181 needed a small change after the IETF Trust was created. This update aligns its templates with the newer copyright notices.

sections.title: The Replacement in Section 3.7
sections.content: In the copyright notice templates in Section 3.7 of RFC 4181, replace every occurrence of The Internet Society with The IETF Trust. This is the specific change made by RFC 4841.
sections.plainLanguage: In each template, use the name The IETF Trust instead of The Internet Society.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that these updates have no impact on the security of the Internet. The document only changes the name used in copyright notice templates.
sections.plainLanguage: The name change does not affect Internet security.
